checks.rationale: The complete three-file diff adds one pure, flat domain-value module, owned tests and handoff. Immutable identity, scope, error, evidence and outcome values remain below side-effect ports; no IO, schema decoder, state writer, adapter, workflow or runtime wiring is introduced. The fresh R2 invocation is distinct from implementation and R1 and uses the user-authorized higher-rank manual review binding described in the report.

ADR-001 flat Python/JSON boundaries, ADR-002 plan-qualified local identity and single writer, ADR-003 isolated candidate lineage, ADR-004 separate exact-candidate review gates, and ADR-005 ownership/injected adapter boundaries are honored. No accepted decision or shared contract changes.

TASK-001 has no prerequisites and PLAN-001 has no accepted/completed engine sibling handoffs to consume. Compatibility with the delivered bootstrap is preserved by an independently observed 24-test pass. Frozen consumer tasks TASK-002/003/004/014/039 retain their own ports, decoding, ownership analysis and orchestration responsibilities.

Public common types supply the frozen port signature needs through explicit domain_values imports. Plan-local RecordRef identity is qualified; EntityId, Revision, EvidenceRef and immutable error/result data support typed owning-port envelopes. No consumer port or request/result class is defined prematurely. ExecutionStatus.tasks_accepted remains distinct from CompletionStatus.completed.

The new API is additive; existing source files, CLI behavior, package entry points and versioned schemas are unchanged. Service-specific statuses remain with their owning envelopes, while ResultEnvelope requires explicit evidence for success and error data for non-success. Exact-file permission containment is preserved despite conservative collision detection.

No schema, stored record, migration or database behavior changes. Candidate-bound R1 evidence compares 21 lifecycle vocabularies directly with v1 schemas. R2 independently verifies unchanged scope wire forms for all 39 tasks and proves the common values can form a schema-valid project event before a plan; typed transaction events need not be looked up as RecordRef. Offline decoding/semantic validation remain TASK-004 work.

Flat src/domain_values.py, task-owned test directory and plan-local handoff follow the declared layout. Names and StrEnum wire values agree with frozen contracts; exact-file versus trailing-separator directory syntax and conservative Unicode/case normalization agree with current scope rules. No root export, package metadata or central registry edit occurs.

TASK-001 owns common immutable values and lexical scope comparisons. It does not duplicate TASK-002/003/039 service protocols, TASK-004 record validation/digests, TASK-014 graph ownership analysis, or the bootstrap installer/CLI. The later ownership task can consume the primitive comparison without transferring its graph, Git-diff or sequencing responsibility.

Logical RecordRef identity, content-addressed EvidenceRef paths, lexical scope values, immutable DomainError and its throwable wrapper have distinct roles. Conflict overlap conservatively detects equality/ancestry without granting descendant access. Project-wide uniqueness, filesystem alias resolution and transaction effects remain later service invariants. No concrete required use case establishes a conflicting abstraction.

The entire test file was independently read: cases exercise qualified identity, portable paths, ancestor conflicts in both access directions, permission boundaries, deep immutability, invalid JSON, exception propagation and evidence requirements. R1 supplies the actual 15-test/90-assertion/schema evidence. R2 adds graph-wide compatibility checks and an actual 24-test bootstrap pass rather than relying on exit-zero discovery alone.

The complete implementation handoff matches candidate behavior, public exports, repaired collision/permission semantics and validation lineage. It distinguishes the pure value module from future services and preserves prior failed review history. The immutable candidate record supplies final exact base/head after metadata merges; this report does not claim TASK-001 is already integrated or that later engine behavior exists.

AC-01/REQ-01 and both task acceptance criteria remain supported without expanding product scope. Approved graph r4 and its structural digest match current tasks/isolation evidence, and all 280 unordered pairs remain disjoint under the repaired comparison. R1 is current for the same fingerprint, all applicable R2 checks pass, and no structural discovery or replan is required. Source/current context differences are CRLF-only and frozen candidate bytes remain verified.
